Experiment_description: Baseline comparison of InterPLM Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) features against raw ESM-2-8M neurons for detecting protein biological concepts (BINDING, ACT_SITE, MOTIF, DOMAIN, MOD_RES annotations) at the residue level using a Swiss-Prot subset (~200 proteins).
Significance: This is the seed baseline establishing whether SAE features learned on top of a protein language model provide better interpretability (via concept alignment) than raw neuron activations. Results here justify subsequent SAE-focused interpretability work by showing SAE features recover substantially more biological concepts than raw neurons, mirroring findings from InterPLM at a smaller scale (ESM-2-8M).
Description: The experiment loads ESM-2-8M and an InterPLM SAE layer, obtains Swiss-Prot annotations (parsing UniProt FT lines for BINDING/ACT_SITE/MOTIF/DOMAIN/MOD_RES) with local-first and REST fallback strategy, extracts residue-level activations for both raw neurons and SAE features on ~200 proteins, and computes per-neuron/per-feature F1 scores by thresholding activations at an optimized per-feature percentile on training residues. Concepts are counted as 'recovered' at F1 >= 0.5. Diagnostic plots evaluate SAE health (activation distribution, sparsity, dead features, reconstruction MSE).

List_of_included_plots.description: Bar chart of feature activation frequency categories (Dead, Very Rare, Rare, Common, Very Common) on log-scale y-axis.
List_of_included_plots.analysis: Shows SAE health: very few dead features and few very-common features, with most in Rare/Common bins. Indicates the SAE dictionary is well-utilized with sparse and specialized features, supporting downstream interpretability claims.

List_of_included_plots.description: Histogram of L0 norm (number of active features per token) with mean ~136 active features.
List_of_included_plots.analysis: With a dictionary width of ~2548, an average of 136 active features/token corresponds to ~5% sparsity. The narrow distribution suggests consistent sparsity behavior — an important diagnostic before interpreting individual features.

List_of_included_plots.description: Distribution of reconstruction MSE between SAE-reconstructed and original ESM-2 activations, right-skewed with mean ~0.577.
List_of_included_plots.analysis: Reconstruction quality is reasonable but imperfect with some hard-to-reconstruct tokens in the tail. Without normalization context, absolute MSE magnitude is hard to interpret, but the shape suggests non-catastrophic reconstruction that supports interpretability analysis.

Key_numerical_results.description: Number of concepts recovered at F1 >= 0.5 by SAE features
Key_numerical_results.analysis: SAE features recover 7x more concepts than raw neurons, demonstrating that sparse dictionary features are substantially more aligned with biologically annotated concepts than raw model neurons.

Key_numerical_results.description: Number of concepts recovered at F1 >= 0.5 by raw ESM-2-8M neurons
Key_numerical_results.analysis: Raw neurons alone barely recover any concept at the F1>=0.5 threshold, consistent with polysemanticity/superposition in dense neural representations.

Key_numerical_results.description: Best per-concept F1 score achieved by SAE features
Key_numerical_results.analysis: Some SAE features achieve strong alignment (F1 ~0.75) with specific biological concepts, indicating high-quality concept-selective features exist.

Key_numerical_results.description: Best per-concept F1 score achieved by raw neurons
Key_numerical_results.analysis: The best raw neuron reaches F1=0.54, showing some concept information exists in individual neurons but is much weaker than in SAE features.
Mean alignment is ~3x that of raw neurons, showing the effect is not driven by a single concept but is systemic across evaluated concepts.
Low mean F1 for raw neurons confirms most concepts have no single strongly aligned neuron.
Provides the denominator for the concept recovery counts; a modest but non-trivial evaluation scope for a baseline.

Key_numerical_results.description: Mean L0 norm (active features per token) in the SAE
Key_numerical_results.analysis: Corresponds to ~5% sparsity relative to dictionary width, an acceptable sparsity regime for interpretability.
Provides a quantitative measure of how faithfully the SAE captures the ESM-2 residual stream; useful baseline for later SAE improvements.
